thread:
incident-bot: ALERT - increase in 5xx rate for service-image-proxy in prod canary · 1938456789

ashley: seeing alerts firing on the canary, short spike in 5xx. anyone rolling things out right now?

raj: I just triggered a canary for service-image-proxy from CI at ~1938456700. Can confirm canary traffic was routed. Notified deploy-bot but not yet promoted.

deploy-bot: deployment started: service-image-proxy:2026-03-15-abc123 -> canary (10%) · job/ci-deploy/8421

maya: logs show image pull errors from some nodes: 
```
failed to unpack image "gcr.io/redwood-prod/service-image-proxy@sha256:7a3f...": unexpected EOF
error: failed to start container
```

ashley: yup getting the same. KCMD: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=service-image-proxy -o wide` shows CrashLoopBackOff on 2/3 canary pods.

raj: can we check the image manifest/digest in registry? sending sha from the CI job: `service-image-proxy:2026-03-15-abc123` resolves to `sha256:7a3f1e9b...` according to CI metadata.

jess: looking at registry: `gcr.io/redwood-prod/service-image-proxy:2026-03-15-abc123` -> points to `sha256:7a3f1e9b...` but node pulled `sha256:4b9d...` on some hosts. that smells like a stale layer/cache mismatch on the registry side or mirror.

maya: could be a garbage/partial push earlier. some container runtimes fall back to cached layers. we saw this before with mutable tags + registry mirrors.

ashley: impact: canary traffic ~10% of prod. small customer-facing errors for image requests proxied by this service. SLOs: increased error budget burn but not widespread. marking as P2 for now unless it spreads.

raj: immediate mitigation options: 1) pause promotion, 2) kill the canary deployment (scale to 0), 3) toggle feature flag to route away from new proxy. which do we want?

maya: do 2 + 3. Kill the canary and flip the flag so clients use the previous path. I've seen flip + redeploy reduce blast radius fast.

ashley: doing kill switch on feature flag: `flags-api set image_proxy_canary=false --env=prod`

deploy-bot: feature-flag change applied: image_proxy_canary=false · actor=ashley · 1938456798

ashley: scaling canary down now: `kubectl -n prod scale deploy service-image-proxy-canary --replicas=0`

maya: confirm pods terminating. health metrics returning to baseline on the next 30s window. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PAGE -> oncall@redwood SRE: new active incident: CANARY_IMAGE_PULL_ERRORS (investigating) · 1938456805

ashley: paging done. tagging this thread as incident for a short postmortem.

raj: collected artifacts: CI job id 8421, pushed manifest digest sha256:7a3f1e9b..., node pull logs show attempted pulls of sha256:4b9d...; registry mirror in eu-west-2 reported io errors around 1938456690-1938456720.

jess: opened ticket with registry team referencing mirror kube-proxy logs and our CI push logs — possible partial push or mirror inconsistency.

maya: for rollback plan: we should re-push immutable-tagged artifact (digest pinned) and force nodes to pull the correct digest. avoid mutable tags for now.

ashley: agreed. short term we stopped traffic. longer term we need guardrails: block promotions if registry mirror lag > 30s and add CI verification that every canary node pulled the expected digest before promoting.

sre-lead: summary for handoff — oncall: ashley. Situation: canary for service-image-proxy started, observed image pull/unpack errors on subset of nodes due to mismatched layer/digest served by registry mirror. Impact: elevated 5xx for ~10% of traffic, mitigated by disabling canary feature flag and scaling canary to 0. Current status: mitigated, no active customer-facing errors. Actions in progress: registry ticket opened (TKT-4247), CI will re-push artifact with immutable digest and run cross-region pull verification, ops will invalidate corrupted mirror cache.

ashley: handing off to next oncall — raj, you'll take the rest of the bridge and follow registry/resolution?

raj: taking it. I'll keep monitoring for 15m then move to a follow-up runbook. next steps: gather all node pull logs (`journalctl -u containerd | grep "sha256"`), run `gcrane ls` on tag vs digest, coordinate with registry team to flush mirror and re-replicate.

jess: also adding a CI gating job to verify digest parity across mirrors before promoting. PR opened: github.com/redwood/ci/pull/987 (draft)

maya: can we draft a customer impact blurb? opscomms may want a short line.

raj: suggested blurb: "We briefly observed increased error rates for image requests routed through a canary deployment of our image proxy due to an artifact replication issue in our container registry. The canary was disabled and traffic reverted; there is no ongoing customer impact. We are investigating the registry replication and will report when resolved."

ashley: good. cc: support and comms.

sre-lead: handoff checklist: 1) ensure registry ticket has owner and ETA, 2) validate re-push and cross-region pull, 3) update CI gating PR, 4) write short postmortem draft for post-incident review.

raj: acknowledged. I'll log progress to TKT-4247 and update this thread. setting follow-up reminder 1938457420 (~10m) to check mirror re-replication.
